look_here_first: LITTLE BARLEY: native cool-season grass with a compact erect spike holding THREE closely grouped spikelets per rachis node, their long fine awns creating a barley-like bristle. Distinguish from Secale cereale by inspecting a single spike node and checking the short annual rooted tuft.

crew_field_check: Secale cereale generally has one large two-flowered spikelet at each alternate node, not a barley triad. Introduced wall barley Hordeum murinum makes broader fan-like spikelet groups. Use floret and glume closeup.
